E0001.title: unclosed form
E0001.explanation: The file ended inside a list, array, table or dotted pair. The location points at the opening delimiter that was never closed. Count delimiters from there, or run `otium fmt` on the file: its indentation usually shows where a closing delimiter went missing.

E0002.title: unterminated string
E0002.explanation: A string literal has no closing double quote before the end of the file. Strings may span lines, so the missing quote can be far above the end of the file. Write `\"` for a double quote inside a string.

E0003.title: unexpected closing delimiter
E0003.explanation: A `)`, `]` or `}` appeared with nothing open to close, or closes a different kind of bracket than the one that is open. Often an earlier form has one closing delimiter too many.

E0004.title: invalid number
E0004.explanation: A token starts like a number but is not one. Otium reads decimal integers, decimal floats with an optional exponent and `0x` hexadecimal integers. A token such as `12abc` is an error, not a symbol. Rational literals such as `1/2` are not supported; write `(/ 1 2)`.

E0005.title: reserved # token
E0005.explanation: Supported # syntax includes booleans, character literals such as `#\a`, and bytevectors such as `#u8(1 2)`. Other # syntax from Scheme or Clojure, such as `#(...)` vectors, `#{...}` sets and `#_` datum comments, is reserved. Use `[...]` for arrays.

E0006.title: invalid string escape
E0006.explanation: Strings accept `\n`, `\r`, `\t`, `\0`, `\e`, `\"`, `\\` and `\xHEX;` escapes, where HEX names a Unicode scalar value and the semicolon ends it. Any other character after a backslash is an error.

E0007.title: malformed dotted list
E0007.explanation: A `.` inside a list must have at least one value before it and exactly one value after it, followed by the closing delimiter.

E0008.title: empty keyword
E0008.explanation: A keyword needs a name after its colon. A bare `:` is not valid.

E0009.title: quote without a value
E0009.explanation: A `'`, backquote, `,` or `,@` must be followed by the form it applies to.

E0010.title: expected value
E0010.explanation: The reader expected a value here and found none.

E0011.title: invalid character literal
E0011.explanation: A character literal needs a character, a supported name such as space or newline, or a hexadecimal Unicode scalar. Surrogates and values above U+10FFFF are invalid.

E0101.title: malformed special form
E0101.explanation: A special form has the wrong number or arrangement of parts, or its argument list is not a proper list. Check the form against its documentation with `(describe 'name)`.

E0102.title: invalid binding list
E0102.explanation: `let` takes a list of `(name value)` pairs: `(let ((x 1) (y 2)) body ...)`. Square brackets build arrays in Otium, so Clojure's `(let [x 1] ...)` is not a binding list. Plain `let` is sequential, so a later binding may use an earlier one.

E0103.title: invalid parameter list
E0103.explanation: Parameters are symbols, each named once. A rest parameter is written `(a . rest)`, `(a & rest)` or as a single symbol. Square brackets build arrays in Otium, so Clojure's `(fn [x] ...)` is not a parameter list.

E0104.title: cannot rebind a core form name
E0104.explanation: Names of core forms such as `if`, `let`, `fn`, `def` and `quote` cannot be used as variable or parameter names. Choose another name.

E0105.title: definition not allowed here
E0105.explanation: `def` is allowed at top level and at the start of a body, such as a function or `let` body. `def-`, `defmacro`, `ns` and `require` are allowed only at top level.

E0106.title: unquote outside quasiquote
E0106.explanation: `,` and `,@` are only meaningful inside a backquoted template.

E0107.title: invalid cond clause
E0107.explanation: Each `cond` clause is a list whose first element is the test: `(test body ...)`. An `else` clause needs a body.

E0108.title: invalid try form
E0108.explanation: `try` takes body expressions followed by `(catch (predicate name) body ...)` clauses. Catch clauses must come after every body expression.

E0109.title: invalid assignment target
E0109.explanation: `set!` assigns a variable, `(set! name value)`, or a callable place, `(set! (object key) value)`. A symbol macro can only be assigned when it has a writer.

E0110.title: invalid ns clause
E0110.explanation: `ns` accepts `(:require spec ...)` clauses after the namespace name. Requires can also be written as separate `(require ...)` forms.

E0111.title: macro expansion limit exceeded
E0111.explanation: Expanding one top-level form ran more than 10000 macro calls. A macro probably expands into a call to itself without making progress. The notes list the most recent macros expanded.

E0112.title: macro transformer failed
E0112.explanation: A macro's own code raised an error while it was building its expansion. The note gives the underlying error. Macros receive unevaluated forms, so the usual cause is a macro that treats a form as a value, or a call that does not match the shape the macro expects.

E0201.title: unbound name
E0201.explanation: No definition, parameter, local binding or import with this name is visible here. Check the spelling, `require` the namespace that defines it, or define it. Many Scheme and Clojure names differ in Otium: use `def` rather than `define` or `defn`, and `fn` rather than `lambda`. Check `(describe 'name)` and the prelude before assuming a familiar function exists.

E0202.title: namespace not found
E0202.explanation: `require` looks for `a/b.ot` for namespace `a.b` under each load path. Add the directory with `-L`, `OTIUM_PATH` or a `(paths ...)` entry in `project.ot`, or fix the namespace name.

E0203.title: name not defined by namespace
E0203.explanation: A `:refer` list or a qualified name names something the namespace does not define.

E0204.title: private name
E0204.explanation: Names defined with `def-` are private to their namespace and cannot be referred to or used qualified from another namespace. Use a public definition or move the code.

E0205.title: circular namespace load
E0205.explanation: Namespace A requires B while B, directly or indirectly, requires A before A has finished loading. Move the shared definitions into a third namespace.

E0206.title: namespace does not match file
E0206.message: file declares namespace `{declared}` but was loaded as `{namespace}`
E0206.explanation: The `ns` form of a file loaded by `require` must name the namespace it was found under: `app/tools.ot` must start with `(ns app.tools)`.

E0207.title: definition conflicts with import
E0207.explanation: A definition and an import in the same namespace may not share a name. Rename the definition, or drop the name from `:refer` and use an alias instead.

E0301.title: wrong number of arguments
E0301.explanation: A function was called with more or fewer arguments than its parameter list accepts. There are no optional or keyword parameters; a rest parameter accepts any number of extra arguments. Check the signature with `(describe 'name)`.

E0302.title: value is not callable
E0302.explanation: The head of a call evaluated to something that cannot be applied. Functions, tables, arrays, keywords and class instances are callable; numbers, strings, `nil` and lists are not. A common cause is extra parentheses around a value, such as `((get t :f))` when `(get t :f)` returns a number.

E0401.title: wrong type of argument
E0401.explanation: A built-in operation received a value of a type it does not accept. Remember that only `nil` and `#f` are false, that `nil` is not the empty list, and that `get` returns `nil` for a missing key.

L0001.name: if-chain
L0001.title: if in the else branch of an if
L0001.message: `if` in the else branch of an `if`; use `cond`
L0001.explanation: Nested ifs in the else position read as a ladder. `cond` lists each test and result at the same depth.

L0002.name: liftable-function
L0002.title: nested function has no captures
L0002.message: `{name}` does not capture enclosing bindings; consider a top-level `def-`
L0002.explanation: A named helper that does not depend on enclosing local bindings can be a private top-level definition. This reduces nesting and makes its independence explicit. Keep it local with a suppression when that makes the code easier to read. This rule checks explicit named function definitions after macro expansion; it skips ambiguous source locations, reassigned helpers and Chez host forms. It does not suggest lifting groups of mutually dependent helpers.

L0101.name: foreign-definition
L0101.title: Scheme or Clojure definition form
L0101.message: `{form}` is not an Otium form; use `{replacement}`
L0101.explanation: Otium defines with `def`, makes functions with `fn` and has a sequential plain `let`. `define`, `defn`, `lambda`, `let*` and `letrec` from Scheme and Clojure are not defined.

L0102.name: bracket-bindings
L0102.title: square brackets used as a binding list
L0102.message: square brackets build an array; `{form}` takes {expected}
L0102.explanation: In Otium `[a b]` builds an array. Binding and parameter lists are parenthesized: `(let ((x 1)) ...)`, `(fn (x) ...)`, `(def (f x) ...)`.

L0201.name: unbound-name
L0201.title: name is not defined
L0201.explanation: After macro expansion, this name is not a local binding, a definition in this file, an import or a prelude name. At runtime it raises E0201.

L0202.name: unused-binding
L0202.title: local binding is never used
L0202.explanation: A `let` binding, parameter or `match` variable is never referenced. Remove it, or start its name with `_` to show it is intentionally unused.

L0900.name: expansion-failed
L0900.title: lint could not expand a form
L0900.explanation: Name checks run on macro-expanded code. The linter loads required namespaces and evaluates the file's own `defmacro` forms, but runs nothing else. A form that fails to expand, for example because a macro depends on a value computed in the same file, is skipped by the checks that need expansion.

L0901.name: unused-suppression
L0901.title: suppression comment suppressed nothing
L0901.message: `{rule}` is allowed here but never reported
L0901.explanation: A `lint: allow` directive names a rule that reported nothing in the code it covers. Remove the directive, or the rule name, so stale suppressions do not hide future problems.

L0902.name: unexplained-suppression
L0902.title: suppression comment without a reason
L0902.message: suppression needs a reason after the rule list
L0902.explanation: Every `lint: allow(rule ...)` and `lint: allow-file(rule ...)` directive must say why, after the closing parenthesis, so readers can judge whether it still applies.
L0902.fixed: ;; lint: allow(if-chain) mirrors the table in specs/io.md

L0903.name: unknown-rule
L0903.title: suppression names an unknown rule
L0903.explanation: A `lint:` directive, or the `lint` entry of `project.ot`, names a rule that does not exist. Run `otium lint --rules` for the list.
L0903.fixed: ;; lint: allow(if-chain) mirrors the spec table
